newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Sept electric futures expire flat to higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Sept electric futures expire flat to higher.

text.p: NYMEX September electricity futures expired flat to higher Tuesday amid steady physical prices in the West and a rash of wildfires burning in various parts of the region, market sources said.
"We're closest to convergence between futures and cash so far," said one Houston trader, noting sometimes wide variances between futures and cash market prices in earlier expirations.

September California-Oregon Border (COB) futures expired down one cent at $18.23 per megawatt hour (MWh) after trading between $17.90 and $18.50. September physcial prices today were quoted at $17.80-$18.20.
Octobr COB settled unchanged at $16.40. Other active COB months finished 10 and 20 cents lower.

September Palo Verde (PV) futures expired up 27 cents at $21.35 per MWh, near its session high of $21.40 after hitting a session low of $20.85. September PV, in the cash market, was assessed in in $21.00-$21.25.
October PV finished up 10 cents at $16.80. Some deferred PV contracts closed up 15 to 30 cents.
Brokers and traders expect October electricity futures to test lower levels, possibly in the mid-$15.00 range, when they debut as the spot contracts Wednesday.
"They'll slip a little more," the Houston trader said.
NYMEX estimated 398 COB and 122 PV lots were sold today.
